scope.flow: Float128::le comparison of the former packed float against the later packed float (former <= later), including mantissa-kind handling
scope.environment: Solidity smart contract (Forte codebase, Float128 library)

statements.text: Float128::le takes two packed floats and is responsible for comparing whether the former is less than or equal to the later.
retVal is determined via the less-than check lt(bMan, aMan) on the mantissas.
At least one of the compared packed floats contains an L Mantissa.
The two packed floats are technically equal in value while being compared.

The mantissas are not of the same kind, since the report states the issue cannot be seen when two packed floats with equal kind of Mantissa are passed, implying the early equals-to-unwrap check does not catch this equality.
Determining retVal via lt(bMan, aMan) fails to consider the equality case when a packed float has an L Mantissa.
Float128::le returns false for technically equal packed floats.
The core comparison functionality of le is broken by this behavior.

A less-than-or-equal-to function must return true for technically equal packed floats; le should consider equality, not only strict less-than. Inferred from the stated responsibility (former <= later) and the claimed omission of equality handling.

ambiguities: The meaning of 'L Mantissa' and 'equal kind of Mantissa' is not defined in the report.
No PoC or concrete input values are given; the specific inputs producing technically equal packed floats with differing mantissa kinds are unspecified.
It is not described how technically equal packed floats with an L Mantissa are produced or reach le.
No attacker or exploit scenario is identified; impact is limited to the le operation returning false on equality.
Downstream consumers of le and their behavior on a false return are not described.
The exact behavior of the early equals-to-unwrap check is not detailed beyond catching equal-kind Mantissa cases.
